name: Thematic growth ETF allocation
heading: The Structural Opportunity: Diversified Thematic Growth
caseLead: The investment case rests on structural spending across automation, clean energy and digital payments, which allows diversified funds to capture growth as technology lowers costs and adoption rises. The opportunity persists because governments support energy security, domestic manufacturing and digital infrastructure, while companies continue investing to protect margins and strengthen supply chains.
caseRest: The main risk is that long-term growth expectations are sensitive to interest rates, so valuations can fall sharply when real yields rise even if revenue continues to grow. Diversification across themes reduces company-specific and policy risk, but it offers less protection when higher discount rates affect all growth assets together. The indicative test returned 12.6% a year with 21.0% volatility, a 46.0% worst fall and return skew of -0.2, showing that losses were larger than a normal distribution would imply.
figNote: The large figure on each card shows the Nasdaq Composite’s return during the calendar month. The index provides a consistent measure of growth equity conditions, with large negative readings signalling pressure from weaker earnings expectations, higher discount rates or falling risk appetite.

events.title: Credit stress drives a growth equity sell-off
events.text: Growth equities fell as the financial crisis restricted credit and reduced corporate investment, sending the Nasdaq Composite down 17.7%. The strategy would have lost because automation, digital infrastructure and clean technology all depended on funding and capital spending.

events.title: Vaccines and policy support lift growth themes
events.text: Growth equities rose after positive vaccine results and the US election improved expectations for reopening and clean-energy policy. The strategy gained because digital payments retained pandemic-led demand while automation and clean-energy funds benefited from stronger investment expectations.

events.title: War compounds inflation and rate pressure
events.text: Russia’s invasion of Ukraine raised energy costs and added to inflation already driving tighter monetary policy. The strategy lost because higher bond yields reduced growth valuations, while supply disruption increased costs for clean-energy and automation companies.

events.title: US subsidies support domestic investment themes
events.text: The US enacted major semiconductor and clean-energy subsidies, improving long-term demand for domestic manufacturing and renewable infrastructure. Results were mixed because policy support helped selected themes, but rising real yields drove the broader Nasdaq Composite down 4.6%.

events.title: Lower inflation expectations revive growth valuations
events.text: Growth equities rallied as softer inflation improved expectations that monetary tightening would slow. The strategy gained because lower bond yields supported valuations across automation, clean energy and digital payments, lifting the Nasdaq Composite by 10.7%.

events.title: Tariffs divide domestic and global themes
events.text: Sweeping US tariff announcements initially reduced risk appetite and raised expected equipment and component costs. Results were mixed because automation and clean-energy supply chains faced margin pressure, while domestic production incentives supported selected companies and the Nasdaq Composite recovered to a small monthly gain.

instrument: Low-cost global ETFs covering automation, clean energy, digital payments and enabling infrastructure
rules: Themes require durable revenue growth, broad company exposure and liquid funds; portfolio rebalanced quarterly and reviewed annually
costs: Estimated fund charges, bid-ask spreads and quarterly rebalancing costs deducted
constructionTitle: Strategy construction, from structural revenue growth to thematic diversification

legs.purpose: Captures industrial automation and labour substitution
Captures electrification, renewable power and grid investment
Captures the shift from cash to electronic transactions
Diversifies exposure across suppliers to several themes
Funds rebalancing and limits forced sales

entry: Allocate at the quarterly rebalance when each theme passes liquidity, diversification and revenue-growth tests
size: Weight themes by risk, with no theme above 30% of the portfolio
exit: Remove a theme when adoption, policy support or revenue growth falls below the annual review threshold
stop: Reduce any theme by half after a 35% fall and a failed fundamental review
marketWatch: Real yields and earnings revisions are the main indicators because thematic valuations depend on both discount rates and expected revenue growth. Semiconductor orders, electricity-grid spending and payment volumes show whether adoption remains strong. Central bank meetings, tariff decisions and industrial-policy announcements are the upcoming events most likely to change valuations or expected investment.

favourable.heading: Falling real yields
favourable.text: Lower real yields favour the strategy because they increase the present value of earnings expected well into the future. This mechanism supported the broad growth rally in January 2023 as inflation eased and expectations for further monetary tightening moderated.

favourable.heading: Capital spending accelerates
favourable.text: Stronger capital spending favours the strategy because automation and infrastructure suppliers gain orders as companies expand capacity and improve productivity. The reopening cycle in 2020 and 2021 supported these themes as manufacturers responded to labour shortages and supply constraints.

favourable.heading: Policy supports investment
favourable.text: Industrial subsidies favour the strategy when they improve project economics and create multi-year demand for equipment, software and components. US semiconductor and clean-energy legislation in 2022 strengthened order expectations even though higher interest rates limited near-term equity returns.

adverse.heading: Real yields rise sharply
adverse.text: Higher real yields hurt the strategy because they reduce growth valuations before changes in revenue or earnings become visible. This effect drove the 2022 drawdown as central banks tightened policy and investors reduced exposure to long-duration equities.

adverse.heading: Subsidies and rules reverse
adverse.text: Policy reversals hurt the strategy when they reduce expected clean-energy projects or restrict access to important export markets. Changes to solar subsidies and trade rules have previously reduced orders, compressed margins and increased volatility across renewable-energy funds.

adverse.heading: Theme valuations become crowded
adverse.text: Crowded valuations hurt the strategy when fund inflows push prices ahead of achievable revenue and earnings growth. Clean-energy and disruptive-technology funds fell sharply after early 2021 as higher yields exposed weak cash flow and excessive valuation assumptions.

infoHist: Historical results show the strategy’s estimated peak-to-trough return during each event using the default thematic weights and quarterly rebalancing rules. Rehyn uses live ETF returns where available and representative sector indices before fund inception, after estimated costs.
infoForward: Scenario results show the estimated return over the first month of each scenario. Rehyn’s scenario engine projects moves in global equities, real yields, energy prices, currencies and thematic valuation multiples, then applies them to the strategy’s current regional and sector exposures.
